state.label: Dormant

confidence.label: Low
confidence.reason: Important mechanisms are unavailable or lack direct evidence.

state.summary: No current demand or positioning gate is confirmed; the October 2 Cohen purchase is outside the Watch's three-day catalyst window, while market, options, short-interest, and borrow evidence are stale or unavailable.

interpretation: GME moves to a dormant squeeze-mechanism state because no current demand or positioning gate is confirmed at this observation time. Ryan Cohen's October 2 open-market purchase of 700,000 shares is a material primary-source corporate catalyst and strengthens the fundamental/corporate thesis, but it is now outside the Watch's three-day current-catalyst gate. Market and options observations remain stale, the September 15 short-interest report is delayed, borrow conditions remain unknown, and there is still no direct evidence of forced covering.

market.note: Price and volume are abnormal relative to recent sessions; neither identifies the buyer or proves covering.

shortPressure.note: The September 15 exchange-reported short position fell materially from the August 31 report. The report is delayed and does not establish current positioning or prove forced covering.

borrowPressure.note: No reliable, freely accessible provider with durable timestamps was available. Missing borrow evidence lowers confidence; it is not treated as normal conditions.

optionsPressure.note: Call-heavy activity and near-price strike concentration are observed. Without a historical options baseline, the system does not label total activity abnormal. Dealer positioning and hedging demand are not directly observed and are not asserted.

catalystPressure.note: Ryan Cohen's October 2 open-market purchase is material corporate-demand evidence, but by this October 6 observation it is outside the Watch's three-day current-catalyst gate.

items.title: GameStop raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance
items.detail: Second-quarter results showed $174.0 million adjusted EBITDA and guidance above $650 million, alongside lower revenue.

supplyPressure.note: Recent issuance and contingent future supply oppose the constrained-supply mechanism. Potential dilution depends on warrant exercise, conversion, financing, and transaction conditions; those are modeled as conditions, not one synthetic diluted-share number.

engines.label: Short pressure
engines.headline: 39.07M shares reported short; -31.45% from prior report
engines.interpretation: The September 15 report materially reduced reported short positioning to about 7.74% of shares outstanding, below the 20% structural gate. Because the report is delayed, it does not establish current exposure or prove covering.

engines.label: Borrow pressure
engines.headline: Fee, availability, and utilization unavailable
engines.interpretation: A crucial stress channel is missing, so confidence is capped.

engines.label: Options pressure
engines.headline: Near-term selected expiries show 12.47× call/put volume
engines.interpretation: Calls dominate the selected expiries and 57% of observed call volume sits within $1.25 of spot, but there is no historical activity baseline and no observed dealer-hedging loop.

engines.label: Market pressure
engines.headline: +5.62% on 1.82× 20-session average volume
engines.interpretation: The tape confirms attention and incremental demand, not the identity or motive of buyers.

engines.label: Catalyst engine
engines.headline: Ryan Cohen bought another 700,000 shares on October 2
engines.interpretation: The primary-source insider purchase strengthens the corporate-demand thesis, but it is outside the three-day current-catalyst gate at this observation and does not establish short covering.

engines.label: Supply / dilution
engines.headline: 504.5M shares outstanding after 55.5M-share note exchange
engines.interpretation: Current and contingent supply is materially less constrained than the historical 2021 setup.

strengthening: Ryan Cohen disclosed an additional 700,000-share open-market purchase on October 2 at a weighted average price of $24.4061.
weakening: The October 2 catalyst has aged beyond the Watch's three-day current-catalyst gate, while market, options, and short-interest evidence are also stale.
unchanged: There is still no direct evidence of forced short covering.
Current and contingent share supply continues to oppose the constrained-supply mechanism.
unknown: Current borrow fee, utilization, and shares available remain unavailable from a reliable free source.
Current short positioning after the September 15 settlement date remains unknown until the next official report.

theses.label: Squeeze thesis
theses.summary: The squeeze thesis is not currently supported by a live gate: the latest CEO purchase is now outside the three-day catalyst window, reported short interest is stale and below the structural threshold, borrow is unknown, and direct covering remains unobserved.
supports: Abnormal market activity remains present in the preserved September 22 observation
Observed calls remain concentrated near the preserved September 22 spot level
contradictions: Fresh reported short interest fell 31.45% and is below the 20% structural gate
Current supply is not tightly constrained

theses.label: Fundamental / corporate
theses.summary: Repeated open-market purchases by Ryan Cohen, including another 700,000 shares on October 2, plus improved profitability guidance and strategic activity strengthen the corporate explanation for demand.
supports: Ryan Cohen bought another 700,000 shares on October 2
Large cash, securities, and eBay position
contradictions: Revenue remains lower year over year
Options activity may be amplifying the move

theses.label: Normal-market / no-squeeze
theses.summary: A corporate/catalyst-led repricing without forced buying remains plausible and currently fits better than a squeeze mechanism because live positioning stress is not confirmed.
supports: Fresh short interest is below the Watch's structural positioning gate
contradictions: Volume is elevated and calls dominate selected expirations

forward: Sustained abnormal price and volume, not a one-session reaction.
Repeated options observations establishing that call activity is abnormal versus its own recent history.
A current borrow observation showing materially rising cost, falling availability, or high utilization.
Independent evidence that short exposure remains trapped while price pressure persists.
backward: Volume normalizes and price acceleration fades after the catalyst.
Fresh short-interest or borrow evidence shows easing rather than stress.
New share supply expands faster than incremental demand.

falsifiers: Fresh short interest falls materially without evidence of disorderly covering.
Borrow remains readily available at ordinary fees during continued price strength.
The move persists only as a corporate repricing with normal liquidity and no positioning stress.
Warrant exercise, conversion, ATM issuance, or transaction financing materially expands tradeable supply.
Options activity normalizes and no feedback-demand evidence emerges.
